reuse.why: Every month-wide action and the new setLastMonthSpending go through getBudgetActionCategories and getAverageBudgetAmount, but the eligibility columns are recomputed by a hand-written SQL query at each site instead of one shared loader (getBudgetData is extended separately).

duplication.why: The same SELECT with the '#fixed' and goal_def CASE expressions is pasted verbatim into setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg, with a sixth variant in getBudgetData.

placement.why: The rule and the sign helper live in budget/actions.ts beside the actions, and the new method is registered in budget/app.ts like its siblings.

scope.why: Focused on the eligibility rule, the new action and the flag, with tests; no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: One filter function is a real improvement, but the rule's inputs (fixed tag, template flag) live in five SQL copies, so the next eligibility change again touches every action, and the includeHiddenGroups policy field is always set equal to includeHiddenCategories.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All month-wide actions call getBudgetActionCategories; none keeps its own hidden/income checks.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated SQL blocks are verbatim copies, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: getBudgetActionCategories takes a policy with includeHiddenCategories and a speculative includeHiddenGroups that every caller sets to the same value; the fixed/template conditions are generic rule terms, but their data comes from per-site SQL copies.
